rows.en: But you never know what might happen. At least learn to move around freely.
Going around the markers adds bonus points, so if you trust your skills, give it a shot.
You must be getting used to the EX-Gear by now. This time, show me how much you've improved.
Some of you have barely touched an EX-Gear, and some of you can probably already fly.
As for the test: carry the container here to the goal within the time limit, and you're done.
Do what you can with the skills you have now.
Besides that, I've placed lots of checkpoint markers and targets again.
Starting the test!
Pass the markers or destroy targets and you'll get bonus points.
Don't dawdle! The test's started!
This is a review of everything so far. You don't need to do it all perfectly. Just do all you can right now.
All right! That'll do!
The test starts now!
All right! The test is over!
Well then, shall we start?
There's still time.
All right, that'll do.
The time limit's closing in.
All right! The test is over!
All right! That's enough!
There's still time.
Time's up.
Time's almost up.
So far, so good.
All right! That's enough!
Try going for the bonus points.
Whoops, time's up.
Good! Keep it up!
You're keeping a nice pace.
I'll explain the Walk mode controls.
rows.notes: 640-711 (Hilda): EX-Gear training-room tutorial. Button names as the voice tutorials already in voice.json (Cross button, D-pad, analog stick); mode names as the corpus (Walk / Hover / Flight mode).

rows.en: Why not go for the bonus points?
rows.notes: bonus pointo wo neratte miru ka: read as Gary suggesting it to the examinee; could also be 'Going for the bonus points, huh?' remarking on what the player does.

rows.en: Push the analog stick down to switch to Walk mode.
Not bad at all.
Up, down, left and right on the D-pad move you forward, back, left and right.
rows.notes: Transcript has houkouki; read as houkou-kii ('D-pad').

rows.en: There's a training machine set up with the targets. Balls fly out of it now and then. Dodge or block them, but deal with them.
rows.notes: Same as row 3103 with 'training machine' for 'volleyball machine'.

rows.en: Special moves: press the D-pad twice quickly in one direction to step. Keep holding it at the end of a step to dash.
Press the Cross button to jump.
Hold the Cross button to float in the air for a short while.
While floating, press the D-pad to move through the air, too.
While dashing, you move faster than normal.
You can dash while floating, too. Practice until you can use it well.
I'll explain the Hover mode controls.
Push the analog stick left or right to switch to Hover mode.
In Hover mode, press left or right on the D-pad to turn, and press the L button to hover.
Pressing the D-pad twice in one direction to step works the same as in Walk mode.
Likewise, keep holding the D-pad at the end of a step to dash.
Hold the Cross button to boost upward.
Boosting up feels like jumping, but in Hover mode you can keep holding the altitude you're flying at.
rows.notes: Transcript writes kankaku as 'interval'; read as kankaku 'feel'.

rows.en: That's the big difference from Walk mode.
To lose altitude, quickly press the Cross button twice and keep holding it to boost downward.
rows.notes: Transcript has kakou ('processing') boost; read as kakou 'downward' boost (as Ranka's pf_rnk/822).

rows.en: Well, just keep drilling it until you're used to it.
After that, switch modes and practice however you like.
I'll explain the Flight mode controls.
Push the analog stick up to switch to Flight mode.
Left and right on the D-pad turn, as in Hover mode, but in Flight mode, up on the D-pad descends and down climbs.
Also, unique to Flight mode, press the Cross button to boost and speed up.
rows.notes: Transcript reads 'press boost with the Cross button'; the Cross button is the boost button (corpus: 'Press the x button to boost and speed up').

rows.en: Also, quickly press up, left or right on the D-pad twice in the same direction to roll that way.
Flight mode is a bit harder, but practice it over and over until you can do it properly.
I'll explain shooting attacks.
To attack, you first need to lock on to a target. Press the R button to lock on to the nearest enemy.
While locked on, press the R button again to switch your lock to another enemy.
Also, hold up on the D-pad and press the R button to lock on to enemy aces and such first.
rows.notes: Transcript has houkouki-ue; read as houkou-kii ue ('up on the D-pad').

rows.en: While locked on, press the Square button to shoot the target you're locked on to.
When shooting, the more directly in front of you the target is, the better your accuracy. Don't forget it.
I'll explain melee attacks.
In Walk or Hover mode, press the Triangle button for a melee attack.
rows.notes: Transcript has howaa mode; read as hobaa ('Hover') mode.

rows.en: Press the Triangle button repeatedly to chain melee attacks. Melee only hits enemies near you, so use it carefully.
For melee, lock on to choose your target, then dash to close the distance.
Also, hold the L button in Walk mode to guard. Don't just attack blindly; watching the enemy and defending matters too.
Today, I've specially borrowed a receiving machine from the volleyball club.
rows.notes: reshiibu mashin: a volleyball machine that fires balls to receive.

rows.en: It's perfect for practicing dodging and blocking incoming balls. Use it freely and practice.
I'll explain cargo hauling.
rows.notes: busshi unpan: 'supply transport'; the corpus tutorial calls the act 'container transport'.

rows.en: You can pick up containers on the ground by locking on and getting close.
And press the Square button to set a container you're carrying down where you are.
But your EX-Gear has to be in Walk or Hover mode to pick up a container, so be careful.
And while you're carrying a container, your hands are full, so you can't shoot or use melee. Be careful.
To work a door switch, you also need to lock on and get close, just like picking up a container.
Hold down on the D-pad and press the R button to lock on to containers and door switches first. Use it well.
This is the training room for practicing basic maneuvers.
rows.notes: Transcript has toreeringu ('trailing') room; read as toreeningu ('training') room.

rows.en: First, I'll explain the EX-Gear's operating modes.
